selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What do the three truths lead all animal species to declare together?
questions.answer: They point all animals together to bear witness that Allah alone is truly God.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of animals presented as collective rather than individual?
questions.answer: Because the argument depends on the agreement of all kinds of animals, which makes the witness broader and stronger.

questions.question: What happened in the traveler’s understanding when he witnessed this scene?
questions.answer: He grasped the meaning fully and clearly.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s response to this vision of the earth?
questions.answer: He fully understood the meaning contained in it.

questions.question: What parts of animals are treated as meaningful signs or expressions?
questions.answer: Their senses, inner capacities, limbs, organs, and bodily tools are all treated as signs.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by the “words” of their limbs and instruments?
questions.answer: It means their bodily structures communicate purpose, function, and completeness.

questions.question: Which divine actions in the passage are connected to will?
questions.answer: Bringing beings into existence, making them, and creating them are linked to will.

questions.question: Why is it important that these forms are described as distinct and varied?
questions.answer: Variety shows creative richness and specific determination for each creature.

questions.question: What two characteristics are given for the resulting forms of these creatures?
questions.answer: Their forms are described as ordered and endlessly varied.

questions.question: What is the main claim made by the combined witness of animals in the passage?
questions.answer: Their united condition and makeup testify to Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What does the phrase “by the consensus” add to the meaning of this witness?
questions.answer: It shows that multiple signs and all kinds of creatures support the same truth together.

questions.question: What did the traveler do after seeing this sign?
questions.answer: He understood its meaning completely.

questions.question: Through what inward features do they bear witness?
questions.answer: Through their senses, capacities, and subtle faculties.

questions.question: Name the three major categories of divine activity mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: Creating, distinguishing and beautifying, and measuring and shaping.

questions.question: What characteristics of these features make them convincing signs?
questions.answer: They are proportioned, organized, complete, and expressive.

questions.question: Why are eggs and sperm mentioned?
questions.answer: They are mentioned to show that many different creatures come from origins that are very similar and limited.

questions.question: What does it teach about their proportions and shapes?
questions.answer: Their forms are measured and fashioned with wisdom.

questions.question: What beginnings are named for the emergence of animal life?
questions.answer: Eggs and sperm drops are named as the beginnings.

questions.question: According to the passage, what united message is being testified to by all species of animals?
questions.answer: That there is no true deity except Allah.

questions.question: What is the function of the three truths mentioned at the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: They work together as supporting proofs that lead to one united conclusion.

questions.question: What role does the traveler play in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: He serves as the observer who recognizes and understands the testimony found in creation.

questions.question: What was the traveler able to do after observing this sign?
questions.answer: He was able to understand its message completely.

questions.question: Why might the passage mention both inner faculties and outward limbs?
questions.answer: To show that both the inward and outward aspects of living beings point to their Creator.

questions.question: What is added by saying their bodily parts are also like “words”?
questions.answer: It shows that their physical design, not just their inner capacities, points to Allah.
